I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash, low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; could you describe when these symptoms started and if they are worsening? To help clarify the pattern, have you noticed any joint pain or a specific rash distribution on your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The clinical presentation of a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities combined with a "facial rash not involving the perioral skin" (often described as a slap-like erythema) alongside viral prodromal symptoms is classic for this condition. The requested lab results are being processed to confirm this suspicion.
